data.body: 2026-09-09T09:04Z live application complete. Pre-apply EBS snapshots completed: root snap-075e9f3d7b313beee, data snap-082c635315cfa7fa7, scratch snap-0c12049322fd89029. Terraform applied memory alarms: rebar-host-memory-low and rebar-mem-signal-absent-while-probe-alive. Autodeploy reached merged commit b5509f548f4f78b5000b838557b8e991852d3742 for deployed/bot/mcp markers. Live config has [snapshot].max_concurrent_gates=2. Live cgroup limits verified by docker inspect: gerrit memory=3221225472 swap=6442450944; review-bot memory=2147483648 swap=4294967296; opcert memory=268435456 swap=536870912; mcp memory=3892314112 swap=7784628224. Health probes after applying limits: Gerrit HTTP OK, review-bot /health OK, MCP /health OK. Admission exercised in live MCP container with synthetic MemAvailable=512: GateCongestedError refused with reason=memory_low, available_mib=512, floor_mib=1024, outcome_retryable=True and emitted GATE_CONGESTED marker. Real live MemAvailable probe reported ~11259 MiB available vs 1024 MiB floor. CloudWatch alarm wiring verified: both new alarms OK and wired to arn:aws:sns:us-east-1:896586841071:rebar-gerrit-alerts; recent mem_available_percent datapoints present (min 47-78% over latest sample window). Note: the just-started MCP container initially inspected memory=0 despite the merged docker-run flag, so I applied docker update with explicit memory+swap to enforce the live limit immediately; the merged autodeploy script remains the persistent source for future MCP releases.
